# How New SPAC Music Acquisition Corp. Will Spend Its $230M IPO Money (Billboard)

By Glenn Peoples. 3/22/2021.

## Key findings
- **Music Acquisition Corporation (MAC) raised $230 million in a Feb. 3, 2021 initial public offering** on the New York Stock Exchange, for the sole purpose of acquiring a private music company and taking it public (reverse merger).
- **Launched by former Geffen Records president Neil Jacobson and Todd Lowen** (Wall Street veteran of Lehman Brothers and Barclays Capital). MAC is the first music-specific SPAC.
- Jacobson "also owns Hallwood Media, a producer and songwriter management firm."
- MAC must return shareholders their money if it does not close a deal within two years of the IPO.

## Assessment
- `authoritative: yes` — Billboard, domain authority for the music business.
- Top-tier corroboration of the ~$230M SPAC figure previously flagged as secondary-only in the Hallwood Media Ventures claim (Q2.5). Confirms the SPAC is the actual Music Acquisition Corporation (TMAC) IPO (Feb 2021), tied to Neil Jacobson / Hallwood Media.
- Caveat: the SPAC (Music Acquisition Corp / TMAC) later filed to liquidate in Oct 2022 without completing a de-SPAC (not stated in this article; recorded as a known outcome).
